Section B: Culture, identity and socialisation

text: In 2004 a researcher began a sociological study into the experiences of stay-at-home fathers.
These fathers had given up the breadwinner role to stay at home and look after the children. The
researcher chose to use unstructured interviews. The researcher believed that unstructured
interviews would be like a conversation.
The study was based in a wealthy area of London. The researcher lived in the area and had been
a stay-at-home father himself. Finding a sample was easy because the researcher knew where
other fathers went with their children during the day. A sample of 16 stay-at-home fathers agreed
Each of the 16 participants was interviewed three times over a two-year period. The interviews took
place in various settings including coffee shops, local parks and participants’ homes. Each
unstructured interview lasted for about two hours.

Section C: Social inequality

text: Societies are diverse but in most societies people experience peer pressure and socialisation.
Sociologists agree that in all societies there are agencies of informal social control that try to ensure
conformity. Gender and ethnicity are important factors in an individual’s social identity.
